blurb_html: Chicken marinated in kombu-dashi and soy, simmered with ginger and onion, set with softly cooked egg over rice.
description: Chicken marinated in kombu-dashi and soy, simmered with ginger and onion, set with softly cooked egg over rice.
equipment_html: Small frying pan, 18–20 cm, with a lid (a small pan keeps the egg in a thick layer)

items.amount_html: 150 g (about 1–2 fillets), 2–3 cm pieces (breast works; cook 1–2 min less)
½ small (~60 g), ends cut off, sliced lengthwise ~5 mm
a 2 cm piece (~8 g), finely chopped
1 bowl (~200 g cooked, from ~80 g raw)
80 ml (or 80 ml water + ¼ tsp dashi powder)

intro_html: “Parent-and-child” rice bowl. The chicken sits in the sauce — kombu, dashi, soy, mirin, sake and sugar — while finely chopped ginger and onion soften in the pan with a pinch of salt. Then the chicken goes in with all of its marinade, gets bound with barely set egg poured in two stages, and slides over hot rice.

mise.items_html: dashi · kombu · soy · mirin · sake · sugar
mise.name: Chicken in marinade

notes.html: The method is yours; these details are my guesses — adjust and tell me: 1 tsp oil for the ginger; marinating 15–30 min; the kombu goes into the pan with the marinade and comes out before the egg; the pan cools ~5 min off the heat before the chicken goes in.

• Cook the breast in the bath first (63 °C, 60–75 min for ~2 cm), then slice it.
  • Skip marinating: after the ginger and onion (step 5), pour in the sauce, bring it to a simmer and add the cooked chicken for just 1 minute — no longer, or it tightens — then go straight to the egg.

• Homemade is best — see niboshi–bonito dashi.
  • Water plus ¼ tsp dashi powder is the quick version; the kombu in the marinade adds depth either way.

• The eggs end up only just set.
  • If anyone eating should avoid undercooked egg, keep the lid on with the heat low for another minute or two until fully set.

siblings.title: Ramen noodles with baked baking soda

steps.body_html:
• Have a bowl of hot rice ready before you start the pan — the egg won’t wait.
  • Start the rice cooker about 45 minutes ahead, or reheat leftover rice until steaming.

how.caption: Scoop the hot rice in loosely with a damp paddle — don't press it down.

steps.title: Rice first

steps.body_html:
• Trim the thigh fillets of any excess fat and cut them into 2–3 cm pieces.
  • In a bowl, stir until the sugar dissolves:
    • dashi 80 ml
    • soy sauce 4 tbsp
    • mirin 1 tbsp
    • sake 1 tbsp
    • sugar 1 tsp
  • Drop in the kombu, then the chicken.
  • Leave it 15–30 minutes (in the fridge if longer).

how.caption: Trim off excess fat, then cut the thigh into 2–3 cm pieces.
Stir soy, mirin, sake and sugar into the dashi until the sugar dissolves; add the kombu, then the chicken.

steps.title: Marinate the chicken

steps.body_html:
• Onion: cut off both ends (root and tip), halve it through the cut ends and peel.
  • Lay each half flat and slice it lengthwise — perpendicular to the cut ends, along the lines — about 5 mm thick. Slicing across the lines gives rings that fall apart; lengthwise slices hold their shape in the pan.
  • Ginger: peel, cut into thin matchsticks, then across into tiny cubes.

how.caption: Onion: cut off both ends — root and tip — then halve it through the cut ends and peel.
Slice lengthwise — perpendicular to the cut ends, along the lines — about 5 mm.
Ginger: peel with a spoon edge, slice thin, cut into matchsticks, then across into tiny cubes.

steps.title: Onion and ginger

steps.body_html:
• Crack the eggs into a bowl and beat loosely — 4–5 strokes with chopsticks, cutting through the whites.
  • You want streaks of white and yolk, not a uniform yellow.

how.caption: Beat loosely — 4–5 quick strokes, cutting through the whites. Stop while streaks remain.

steps.title: Beat the eggs

steps.body_html:
• Small pan, the oil, medium-low heat.
  • Drop in the ginger for ~30 seconds until fragrant, then add the onion and a pinch of salt.
  • Stir until the onion is a bit soft — 2–3 minutes, no colour.

how.caption: Ginger first, ~30 seconds in the oil until fragrant.
Then the onion and a pinch of salt; stir until a bit soft.

steps.title: Ginger, then onion

steps.body_html: Take the pan off the heat and let it cool for a few minutes while the chicken finishes marinating.
steps.title: Let it cool down

steps.body_html:
• Back on medium.
  • Tip in the chicken with all of its marinade (kombu too), spread it in a single layer.
  • Bring to a simmer, cover, and simmer, turning once, until cooked through with no pink inside.

images.alt: Chicken in, with all the marinade

how.caption: Back on medium: tip in the chicken with all of its marinade, kombu too.
Halfway through, turn each piece once — the cooked side is opaque white.

steps.title: Chicken in, with all the marinade

steps.body_html:
• Fish out the kombu.
  • Drizzle about two-thirds of the egg in a circle over the chicken and onion.
  • Cover and cook until the egg at the edges is set but the top is still runny.
steps.title: Pour ⅔ of the egg

steps.body_html:
• Pour the remaining egg, cook 10–15 seconds, then turn off the heat and cover for 30 seconds.
  • The egg should be glossy and just set.
  • Cook a little longer covered if you prefer it firm.

how.caption: Pour the last third into the middle, where the egg is thinnest — then heat off, lid on.

steps.title: Pour the rest, heat off

steps.body_html:
• Tilt the pan and slide everything, broth included, over the rice.
  • Top with spring onion greens or mitsuba and a shake of shichimi.

how.caption: Tilt the pan over the rice and slide everything out in one go, broth included.
Finish with sliced spring onion and a light shake of shichimi.

steps.title: Slide onto the rice

timeline.note_html: If your rice is already cooked, skip the first bar — about 35 minutes, most of it the chicken marinating.

tasks.label: Pour ⅓ egg, heat off, rest
